newsitem.title: PERU: U.S., Canada, Latin central bankers meet in Peru.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Canada, Latin central bankers meet in Peru.

text.p: Central bankers from the United States, Canada, Spain and Latin America Wednesday opened two days of talks in Lima to discuss capital flows, inflation and banking regulation.
Participants said they would discuss all aspects of monetary policy, as well as boosting banking cooperation among their countries.
"The goal is to exchange ideas and information. We don't have a strict agenda," Colombia's Central Bank governor Miguel Urrutia told Reuters.

However, organizers said that in the past few years meetings have tended to focus on fighting inflation, the effects of capital flows on the economies of member countries and on ways to harmonize banking regulations.
Capital flows returned to Latin America in the 1990s as most governments in the area adopted free market policies and launched ambitious privatization drives that fostered stability and growth.

But the region has also been concerned about keeping foreign capital and seeking ways to avert major financial disruptions, like the Tequila effect that followed Mexico's December 1994 devaluation and jolted all of Latin America.

Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori promised in an opening speech to press on with free market and austerity policies he implemented in 1990 to fight runaway inflation and build up foreign reserves, currenty at $9.3 billion from a negative $105 million when he took office in 1990.

U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips, Bank of Canada's Deputy Governor Timothy Noel, Bank of Spain's Deputy Governor Miguel Martin and central bank presidents or deputies from Latin America were taking part in the talks behind closed doors.
The officials were holding two separate meetings -- one of central bankers from the Americas, and another of central bankers from Latin America and Spain.
The central bankers from the Americas meet every year and those from Latin America and Spain every six months. Officials from Germany's Bundesbank were also taking part as observers.
